summary: The candidate captures the paper's main degree-theoretic chain, including degree zero implying null-homotopy, the extension theorem, the Hopf degree theorem, and the Euler-characteristic criterion for nonvanishing vector fields. Most extracted formulas have balanced LaTeX and plausible page locators. However, several statements omit essential hypotheses, the torus Euler-characteristic calculation is false, the punctured-space identification is imprecisely presented as a homeomorphic identification, and overlap between extraction chunks creates numerous duplicated entries with inconsistent classifications. Coverage of the Gold supporting infrastructure is incomplete, especially the local degree lemmas, transversality results, vector-field index definition, and the homotopy-group corollary.
strengths: The degree and winding-number definitions are substantially represented, with the central degree formula preserved.
The candidate captures the core Hopf theorem on page 8 in a form that specializes to the Gold self-map classification.
The degree-zero, boundary-extension, range-adjustment, and general extension results preserve most of the proof architecture behind the main theorem.
The vector-field application includes finite-zero, localization or zero-removal, Poincare-Hopf, nonvanishing-field, sphere Euler-characteristic, and hairy-ball entries.
Several imported background results are explicitly marked external, including isotopy, linear isotopy, Sard, the epsilon-neighborhood theorem, and Poincare-Hopf.
Entry IDs and page numbers are generally coherent, and no pervasive LaTeX-delimiter corruption is present.
issues: The entry paper:calculation:torus-euler-characteristic asserts $\chi(T^k)=-2(k-2)$, whereas the Gold reference correctly gives $\chi(T^k)=0$; this is a substantive mathematical error.
The winding-number definition fixes the direction map's codomain as $S^1$, making it dimension-specific where the relevant general construction should land in the appropriate sphere.

The Poincare-Hopf statement omits the requirement that the zeros be isolated or finite, so its displayed sum is not defined for an arbitrary smooth vector field; its page locator also differs from the Gold locator.
The nonvanishing-vector-field theorem omits the boundaryless condition and adds unnecessary connectedness and orientability restrictions, so it does not faithfully preserve the Gold theorem's scope.

The entry named as a homeomorphic identification of punctured spaces uses $\mathbb R^{k+1}\setminus\{p\}\simeq S^k$ without distinguishing homotopy equivalence from homeomorphism, and a separate page-5 stereographic-projection entry has a vague and inaccurate description.
The hairy-ball entry covers only $S^2$, while the Gold result covers every positive even-dimensional sphere and also records existence in odd dimensions.

The candidate omits distinct Gold entries for the vector-field index, the regular-point local winding number, the signed-preimage summation formula, the transversality extension theorem, the transversality homotopy theorem, and $\pi_k(S^k)\cong\mathbb Z$.
The circle base case is weakened to the degree-zero case and omits both equal-degree classification and the standard representatives $z\mapsto z^n$.

Chunk overlap produces repeated entries for boundary extension, degree-zero sphere maps, the circle base case, finite-zero vector fields, zero-index removal, and the Euler/nonvanishing-field theorem; duplicates are sometimes classified inconsistently as theorem versus lemma.

Some background entries are only skeletal: the Sard entry does not state density or the measure-zero critical-value conclusion, and the bump-function entry does not retain the Gold support and plateau conditions.

entryLevelComparison.notes: The intersection-number definition and signed-preimage interpretation are preserved.
The normalization formula is present, but the codomain is incorrectly fixed as $S^1$.
The mathematical implication is correct, but it is extracted twice with different entry types.
The candidate gives the standard degree-zero extension criterion for a boundary map into $S^k$ on a general oriented manifold.

The candidate states the broader source form for maps from a compact connected oriented $k$-manifold to $S^k$, which includes the Gold sphere self-map case, though the no-boundary convention is not explicit.
No entry records the based corollary $\pi_k(S^k)\cong\mathbb Z$ for $k\geq1$.
External attribution and the index-sum formula are present, but isolated or finite zeros and the boundaryless hypothesis are omitted.
The equivalence is captured twice, but both versions omit the no-boundary condition and impose stronger orientability or connectedness assumptions.
The sphere calculation is correct, but the torus calculation is false.
Only the two-sphere case is extracted; the full even-sphere assertion and odd-sphere contrast are absent.
The signed-preimage formula for winding number or degree is not isolated as an entry.
The transversality result needed to justify perturbing vector fields to finite isolated zeros is not extracted.
